title: Dart Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: main is where this Dart program starts. print shows a value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Dart enters main and calls print with the greeting String. Keep the main function around the steps.

exercises.question: var lets Dart work out a type from a value. Numbers can be added with +. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The starting value makes pencils an int. Adding 2 produces 5. A variable set to an int cannot later hold text.

exercises.question: final means a name can be assigned only once. It helps protect a value from accidental changes. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: final accepts one assignment. Reading days gives the stored 7. final prevents reassignment, not every change inside a mutable object.

exercises.question: A dollar sign places a variable inside a Dart string. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: $name becomes Ravi inside the string. The other characters stay unchanged. Use ${...} to insert a calculation.

exercises.question: if checks a Boolean rule. The else branch runs when that rule is false. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The test is true for score 8. The else block is skipped. A number by itself is not a Boolean condition.

exercises.question: A List keeps values in order. add places a new value at the end. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: add puts 8 after 4 and 5. The list then has three items. The first position in a List is zero.

exercises.question: for-in reads each value of a list in order. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: pet receives cat, then dog. The print runs once per item. The loop variable holds one item at a time.

exercises.code:
int twice(int n) => n * 2;
void main() { print(twice(4)); }
exercises.question: A function gives a calculation a name. The arrow form returns one expression. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The arrow expression returns twice the supplied input 4. The returned value must fit the declared type.

exercises.question: A Map pairs keys and values. It can find a value by a text label. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The title key selects one value from the Map: Moon Trip. A missing map key gives null.

exercises.question: String? can hold text or null. ?? chooses a fallback when the value is null. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: name starts as null. The ?? operator supplies Guest. Using ! on null causes an error.

exercises.question: A class is a plan for objects. Its constructor fills in the starting fields. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The constructor stores its input in title. Dot access reads Moon Trip. Use the constructor inputs in the right order.

exercises.question: A Future represents a result that may arrive later. await reads that result inside an async function. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The Future completes with 8. await obtains it before print runs. await belongs in an async function.
